title: Margince installation config (margince.yaml)
$comment: Written by tools/gen-config from the settings registry; do not edit.

workspace.description: Workspace names the installation's singleton workspace — the tenant every row is filed under, and what the schema has always called it. Consumed only when the workspace is created; it never reconciles into an existing installation.

name.description: Name is the company's name until an admin saves the company profile.

base_currency.description: BaseCurrency is the currency every amount is reported in, as a 3-letter ISO 4217 code in capitals, such as EUR.

base_language.description: BaseLanguage is the language the installation writes in, one of those this build speaks.

timezone.description: Timezone is the IANA zone the installation's calendar days are in, such as Europe/Berlin.

country.description: Country is the jurisdiction the installation runs under, as a lower-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code naming a compiled-in pack. Empty leaves it unset. Seeded once, also into an existing installation that has none stored; after that Settings → Jurisdiction changes it, never this file.

bootstrap_admin.description: BootstrapAdmin identifies the first administrator. The password is a reference so the secret can be deleted after first boot — once the workspace exists this whole section may be removed.

password.description: Password is the reference form: ${file:...} or ${env:...}.

password_file.description: PasswordFile is the original spelling, still honoured so an existing deployment boots unchanged. It is a bare path rather than a reference, which is why it is not a Secret: it names a file and cannot name the environment. Prefer `password`.

seeds.description: Seeds externalizes the workspace defaults bootstrap previously seeded from code. Every key is optional — an omitted key seeds the built-in default, so a minimal file behaves exactly like the historical bootstrap. Values are consumed once, at company creation.

pipeline.description: PipelineSeed configures the default pipeline's open stages. Won/Lost terminal stages are appended by the deals module — stage semantics are a module invariant, not an operator choice.

stages.description: PipelineStage is one configured open stage: display name + win probability.

consent_purposes.description: ConsentPurpose seeds one row of the consent purpose catalog.

retention.description: RetentionSeed selects the retention POSTURE a fresh installation is bootstrapped into. It does not select the policy rows: bootstrap plants the same built-in rows under either posture. So an installation that must keep everything still SEES the ladder it is not running.

default_policy.description: DefaultPolicy is `standard` or `retain_only`. Empty means standard, which is the historical behaviour byte for byte.

legal_review.description: LegalReview set to false starts the installation with legal review switched off. Omitted or true leaves the default, which is on.

ai_routing.description: AIRouting is the tier→model binding a fresh installation is bootstrapped with, so a deployment can declare which vendor it uses in the file it reviews rather than having to call an API after first boot. Consumed exactly once, like every other seed here; the database is authoritative afterwards and an admin re-points a lane through /v1/ai/routing.

follow_up_after_days.description: Days a sent message may go without a reply before its sender is asked to follow up.

addr.description: Listen address of the HTTP server.

budget.description: The monthly AI token budget of the company, as tokens_per_full_user and company_monthly_tokens (null for the total over its users).

capture_payloads.description: Keep each AI call's request and answer in ai_call_payload, aged by its retention policy; set it on the api and the worker together.

price_sync.description: Whether the daily job syncs model prices, as {"auto_sync": true|false}. Refresh now runs either way.

provider_keys_anthropic.description: BYOK API key for the Anthropic provider; required only when a binding names it.

provider_keys_gemini.description: BYOK API key for the Gemini provider; required only when a binding names it.

provider_keys_gemini_vertex.description: BYOK service-account key (the JSON key file's contents) for the gemini_vertex provider; required only when a binding names it.

provider_keys_jev.description: API key for the TypeSafe decision provider; required only when the decisions lane binds it.

provider_keys_jev_compatible.description: API key for a jev_compatible decision server; sent when set and never required.

provider_keys_openai.description: BYOK API key for the OpenAI provider; required only when a binding names it.

provider_keys_openai_compatible.description: BYOK API key for the openai_compatible provider; required only when a binding names it.

routing.description: The tier-to-model binding, in the shape seeds.ai_routing takes (JSON in the environment). Unset binds no models.

task_overrides.description: Each task's thinking level and timeouts, as the JSON object PUT /ai/task-overrides takes. Unset keeps the product's values.

ai_fake.description: Drive the AI surfaces with the offline fake model when nothing else can serve (dev and test only).

ai_routing.description: Ignored; kept so existing command lines parse.

performance_enabled.description: Ignored; kept so existing files load.

api_base_url.description: External base of the api for the OAuth redirect_uri when the api and the SPA are on different origins; defaults to --public-base-url.

enabled.description: Email and password sign-in; an installation behind its own identity provider turns it off.

blobstore_access_key.description: Access key for the object store.

blobstore_endpoint.description: Endpoint of an object store such as MinIO for attachment bytes; it wins over MARGINCE_BLOBSTORE_PATH, and with both unset the attachment endpoints answer 501.

blobstore_path.description: Directory attachment bytes are written to when there is no object storage service; ignored when MARGINCE_BLOBSTORE_ENDPOINT is set.

blobstore_secret_key.description: Secret key for the object store.

blobstore_use_ssl.description: Reach the object store over TLS.

auto_enrich.description: Read a new contact's company web page automatically.

auto_enrich_daily_cap.description: Automatic company web-page reads the installation may start in one UTC day.

confidentiality_pass_cap.description: Held mail threads one review pass may judge; the rest wait for the next pass.

freemail_extra.description: Ignored, with a warning at boot; the consumer-mail list is edited under Settings.

freemail_never.description: Ignored, with a warning at boot; the consumer-mail list is edited under Settings.

mail_sharing.description: Let every colleague who can see a contact read the email captured with them; off keeps new mail to those on it.

mail_sync_interval_seconds.description: Seconds a working mailbox connection waits between polls.

max_backfill_months.description: How far back a mailbox import may reach, for the whole installation; 0 is no cap.

shared_posture_allowed.description: Allow a seat to share their mailbox with colleagues as mail lands; turn it on only where a works agreement allows it.

signature_enrich.description: Read contact details from the signatures and attached cards of captured mail, for every mailbox that has made no choice of its own.

site_read_max_mib.description: MiB one company web-page read may hold, over all its pages.

site_read_max_pages.description: Pages one company web-page read may fetch.

site_read_wall_seconds.description: Seconds one company web-page read may run before it stops and extracts what it has.

skip_reserved_domain_proposals.description: Raise no contact proposal for a sender on an RFC 2606 reserved name; the mail is still captured.

trace_payloads.description: Keep each traced message's sender and a bounded subject in the 24-hour capture trace, dropped messages included.

transactional_extra.description: Domains of mail services added to the built-in list; their mail keeps the activity and derives no counterparty.

transactional_never.description: Domains never held back as system mail, whatever the built-in rules say.

certlog_base_url.description: Base URL of a certificate log, or public for a free public one; unset makes no outbound lookups of what a company runs.

rollout.description: Company-context stage: off, read (reads and settings), tasks (AI tasks get it) or onboarding (the first-run flow too).

connector_state_key.description: HMAC key of at least 32 bytes signing the OAuth connect state; required for the Gmail and Graph connect flows.

authorization_modes.description: How strictly the authorization engine applies its answer for each message category: observe, warn or enforce.

controller_particulars.description: Who this installation is, as every message it sends must say: legal name, address, privacy contact, how to object, and advertiser contact.

first_response_enabled.description: Track a first-response target on every lead.

first_response_target_minutes.description: Minutes a lead may wait for its first real response once its clock starts.

signature_template.description: The email signature of the workspace, used in place of the own signature of each sender; empty means none.

unassigned_escalation_user_id.description: The user id of the colleague who answers for a lead nobody owns, or whose owner has left, once it misses its target; empty means nobody, and a boot value that names no active colleague reaches nobody and logs a warning.

pace.description: Delay between saved batches of data tasks.

legal_review_enabled.description: Let a deal be sent to legal for review, and let a legal_reviewed criterion hold a deal at its stage.

maintenance_writes_enabled.description: Let the nightly close-date sweep write to a deal. Off stops every automatic write the sweep makes.

stage_autopilot_enabled.description: Let a deal move to the next stage by itself where the rule of its stage allows it; off stops every automatic move.

dsn.description: Postgres DSN of the runtime app role; migrate falls back to it when MARGINCE_OWNER_DSN is unset.

enabled.description: Send the installation's own mail through the SMTP relay below; needs --public-base-url.

from_address.description: Sender address of the installation's own mail; required when email.enabled.

host.description: SMTP relay host; required when email.enabled.

password.description: SMTP relay password, sealed into the key vault at boot; ${none} deletes the sealed copy and sends without one.

password_file.description: Path to a file holding the SMTP relay password; a password set by reference wins over it.

port.description: SMTP relay port, 1 to 65535 when email.enabled.

username.description: SMTP relay user; unset sends without signing in.

geocode_base_url.description: Nominatim base URL; unset or public uses the public service, off stops the lookup of map points; give the api and the worker the same value, or a lookup is never queued.

gmail_client_id.description: Google OAuth client id of the Gmail capture connector.

gmail_client_secret.description: Google OAuth client secret of the Gmail capture connector.

gmail_jwks_url.description: Override of the Google OIDC JWKS URL, for test and dev.

gmail_pubsub_topic.description:
Gmail Pub/Sub topic (projects/

/topics/) that enables the push-watch job; unset leaves capture on the poll.

gmail_push_audience.description: OIDC audience the Pub/Sub push subscription mints tokens for.

gmail_push_service_account.description: Google service account email that signs the Pub/Sub push OIDC tokens.

gmail_push_token.description: Shared secret on the Pub/Sub push URL; unset, POST /webhooks/gmail is absent.

graph_client_id.description: Microsoft Entra app id of the Outlook and Microsoft 365 capture connector.

graph_client_secret.description: Microsoft client secret of the Outlook and Microsoft 365 capture connector.

graph_notification_url.description: Public URL, token included, that Microsoft posts Graph change notices to; unset leaves Outlook capture on the poll.

graph_push_token.description: Shared secret on the Graph change notice URL; unset, POST /webhooks/graph is absent.

graph_tenant.description: Microsoft identity tenant of the capture consent endpoint and token refresh; unset means common.

enabled_oidc_providers.description: The sign-in providers offered, as a list of provider keys; unset offers every provider the deployment set up.

oauth_dynamic_registration.description: AI tools may register their own OAuth client (DCR) for new sign-ins.

oauth_metadata_documents.description: AI tools may sign in with a client ID that is the URL of their metadata document (CIMD).

oidc_group_role_map.description: The role each directory group grants at sign-in, as group:role pairs; it only grants, and never removes a role.

require_mfa.description: Every member must use two-step sign-in.

require_sso.description: Members other than admins sign in only through a sign-in provider.

inline_relay.description: Run the outbox relay in this process; false when cmd/worker runs it.

agent_calls_per_window.description: Calls of any kind, tool or API, one agent passport may make per window.

agent_egress_per_window.description: Calls that send something out of the workspace one agent passport may make per window.

agent_runner_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the passes of the agent scheduler.

agent_window_hours.description: Hours in the window the agent limits count over; set at boot, it also keeps a length an admin saved for the next reset from taking over.

agent_writes_per_window.description: Changing calls one agent passport may make per window.

base_language.description: The language AI writes the shared record in: en, de or vi.

call_telegram.description: Show a Telegram chat link next to a contact's phone number that starts with a country code.

call_whatsapp.description: Show a WhatsApp chat link next to a contact's phone number that starts with a country code.

call_zalo.description: Show a Zalo chat link next to a contact's phone number that starts with a country code.

country.description: Where the installation is established, as a two-letter ISO 3166-1 code in small letters; empty for none.

date_format.description: How dates are written: locale, dmy, mdy or ymd.

dead_work_banner_hours.description: Hours the job-health banner looks back before it calls dead work a problem.

fiscal_year_start_month.description: The month the business year begins, 1 to 12.

follow_up_reconcile_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the follow-up reconcile passes.

forecast_forward_measure.description: Which remaining-pipeline reading a projected landing is built from.

geocode_backfill_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the sweeps that add missing map points, or 0 for off.

gmail_watch_renew_within_hours.description: Hours before a Gmail push subscription ends that it is renewed.

gmail_watch_scan_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the scans for Gmail push subscriptions due for renewal.

graph_watch_renew_within_hours.description: Hours before a Microsoft Graph mail subscription ends that it is renewed.

graph_watch_scan_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the scans for Microsoft Graph mail subscriptions due for renewal.

name.description: The company's name. Set at boot, it also refuses a different name on the company profile.

oauth_access_token_ttl_minutes.description: Minutes an access token from the OAuth handshake of a connector lives, for the first token and every refresh.

send_max_age_hours.description: Hours a delivery held back by the send rate may wait before it stops with a reason.

send_rate_limit.description: Messages one mailbox may send per send-rate window.

send_rate_window_seconds.description: Seconds in the window the send rate is counted over.

technical_backfill_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the sweeps that add missing technical profiles, or 0 for off.

time_format.description: How times of day are written: locale, 24h or 12h.

webhook_retry_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the passes that retry failed webhook deliveries.

automatic_lookup.description: Look each new contact up once against the connected data provider for the free details, with no request from a user.

job_drain_window.description: How long a running job gets to finish at shutdown; the grace period must cover it, five more seconds and the shutdown steps.

keyvault_root_key.description: Standard Base64 of the 32-byte root key that seals connector credentials; unset disables the vault.

token.description: Licence token; unset with no license.token_file runs with no license, which production refuses.

token_file.description: Path to a file holding the licence token, read again at each licence check; license.token wins over it.

enabled.description: Live Lists and Shortlists; false hides every list surface and deletes no list.

dynamic.description: Let AI tools register their own OAuth client at /oauth/register (DCR); false keeps it off whatever the admin's switch in Settings > MCP says.

metadata_document.description: Accept a client ID that is the URL of the tool's published metadata document (CIMD); false keeps it off whatever the admin's switch in Settings > MCP says.

connector_enabled.description: Serve /mcp and the OAuth authorization server to outside agent clients; needs --public-base-url.

mcp_apps_base_url.description: Origin the api reads the MCP App view documents from; defaults to --public-base-url.

metrics_access.description: Who /metrics serves: token requires --metrics-token, open serves any client that reaches the port.

metrics_token.description: Bearer credential /metrics requires; unset, /metrics refuses every scrape unless --metrics-access=open.

microsoft_signin_tenant.description: Comma-separated Entra directory ids whose members may sign in; defaults to --graph-tenant when that names a directory.

observe_addr.description: Address the worker serves its /healthz, /readyz and /metrics on, such as 127.0.0.1:9101; unset serves nothing.

observe_pprof.description: Serve the Go profiles under /debug/pprof/ on the --observe-addr listener with no sign-in; turn it on only to find a fault.

allow_data_reset.description: Arm POST /v1/admin/reset-data, which purges this installation's tenant data back to its first-boot state.

allow_test_mailbox.description: Arm the test_mailbox connector, a no-network fake mailbox that captures and sends; never on a real deployment.

owner_dsn.description: Postgres DSN of the owner role, which migrate applies the schema with.

retain_only.description: Keep everything: the nightly retention pass erases nothing and strips no personal data, whatever a policy says.

provider_surfe.description: Enrichment provider: live, offline or off; an unknown value fails the boot.

public_base_url.description: External scheme and host for the links a buyer sees and for the OAuth callback; required to send mail.

fx_currencies.description: ISO 4217 codes the FX refresh offers for an empty rate sheet; unset offers USD, GBP and CHF.

fx_source.description: Page the FX refresh reads rates from; unset reads a free source of ECB rates.

model_pricing.description: Ignored, with a warning at boot; kept so existing files load.

redis.description: Redis address of the event bus.

redis_password.description: Event-bus credential, where the Redis server requires one.

schema_dsn.description: Postgres DSN of the owner role for custom-field schema changes; unset, those two operations answer 501.

trusted_proxies.description: Comma-separated CIDR prefixes of the reverse proxies whose client address header the rate limits per IP trust.

attachment_mb.description: Largest request POST /v1/attachments takes, in decimal MB.

csv_import_mb.description: Largest request POST /v1/imports/sources and the vCard import take, in decimal MB.

knowledge_document_mb.description: Largest document POST /v1/knowledge/corpora/{id}/documents takes, in decimal MB.

linkedin_import_mb.description: Largest request POST /v1/me/linkedin-connections takes, in decimal MB.

vat_check_base_url.description: VIES base URL, or public; set it on the api and the worker together, or a VAT check is never queued.

security_txt.description: RFC 9116 security.txt: one or more contact URIs and an RFC 3339 end time, with an optional policy link and preferred_languages.

webhook_key.description: Base64 32-byte key sealing outbound-webhook signing secrets; unset, the webhook paths that change data answer 503 and the worker sends nothing.

work_dir.description: Directory where the AI task probes of the worker write their files.

aiRouting.description: The tier-to-model binding a fresh installation is bootstrapped with. Consumed ONCE, at bootstrap: a running installation is rebound through Settings -> AI, and editing this afterwards changes nothing until the database is rebuilt.

profile.description: Location ladder: eu_hosted (partner EU inference), sovereign (zero egress — cloud providers refused), cloud_frontier (BYOK cloud).

tiers.description: Capability tiers; bind each to one provider. An unbound tier is legal — the router degrades honestly.

embeddings.description: The embedding lane, bound separately from chat (retrieval must survive a chat-budget exhaustion). Required.

decisions.description: The decision-model lane. Optional: absent, every call is the task's own ladder. Present, a task that declares a decision form is asked it first, on a certified site, and falls back to its ladder whenever the answer does not stand.

providers.description: Provider name to what that provider is configured with, independent of any lane: its host and the broker's upstream pins. Every lane binding a provider reads them from here, so a host is written once. A lane's own base_url or pins (the older spelling) are lifted here when the provider names none.

providerSettings.description: One provider's configuration. An entry no lane binds is held to its shape only.

base_url.description: Where the provider is reached. REQUIRED on openai_compatible while a lane binds it (the vendor host root, NO /v1), and on jev_compatible while the decisions lane binds it (the FULL decision endpoint, posted to as written). Empty ⇒ the adapter's compiled default.

upstream.description: openai_compatible on an OpenRouter host only: which upstream hosts may read this provider's requests, and under what privacy — only, ignore, allow_fallbacks, zdr, data_collection, enforce_distillable_text. Every lane on the provider is served under them; how each tier is served (sort, quantizations, latency) stays on its own routing.

location.description: gemini_vertex only, and REQUIRED while a lane binds it: the Vertex AI location that serves the call and processes the prompt — eu, us, global, or a region such as europe-west4.

provider.description: fake | anthropic | ollama | vllm | openai_compatible | openai | gemini | gemini_vertex. The only place vendor names appear.

model.description: Provider-native model id. ollama/vllm default to a Gemma-class model when omitted (A23).

base_url.description: Deprecated here: set the host on providers.<name>.base_url. Still accepted, and lifted onto the provider when it names none.

location.description: Deprecated here: set the location on providers.gemini_vertex.location. Still accepted, and lifted onto the provider when it names none.

input.description: What the bound model can be GIVEN. On openai_compatible/vllm it is the whole answer (the carriage depends on which model was bound). On every other provider it NARROWS the carriage fixed in that adapter's wire — at most what the wire carries, at most what is declared — so it can take image away from a gemini tier and can never add a lane a wire lacks. Omit to take whatever the provider carries; write [text] to send it no attachments. Must include text.

thinking_level.description: How deeply a gemini or gemini_vertex tier thinks when the request names no level of its own. Omit it for the adapter's default: a structured request thinks at low, and a Flash-Lite keeps its own shallower default (minimal), which low RAISES. Gemini charges thinking to the same output ceiling as the answer. Gemini 3 or later only — a Gemini 2.5 answers the field with a 400, and gemini-3.1-pro-preview refuses minimal.

routingNeedsOpenRouter.description: A routing block is OpenRouter's own fields, so a lane may declare one only when it is an openai_compatible binding, and a base_url it still writes must be an OpenRouter host. One clause for both lanes, so the chat tiers and the embeddings lane cannot come to disagree about which host that is. The host usually lives on providers.openai_compatible, which this schema cannot follow; the parser checks the resolved host. The pattern is case-insensitive because URL hosts are, and the parser lowercases the host before it compares.

upstreamRouting.description: How OpenRouter serves this tier: OpenRouter's own request fields, provider (which hosts and how) and reasoning (how hard the model thinks). OpenRouter fronts many inference hosts per model, and its own default picks among them weighted by the inverse square of price — so one model id is served at fp4 on one call and at bf16 on the next, with latency to match. Valid ONLY on an openai_compatible binding whose base_url is an OpenRouter host. OMIT the block to inherit the product default (sort: throughput, quantizations: [fp16, bf16], require_parameters: true — reliability over price); write an empty object to opt out and take the broker's own price-weighted routing. The host filters and privacy keys (x-placement: connection) are set on providers.openai_compatible.upstream; a seed that writes them on a tier has them lifted there, and the settings API refuses them on a tier unless they repeat the connection's own. The older flat spelling (upstreamRoutingFlat) is still read.

openRouterProvider.description: OpenRouter's provider request object. Each key is sent as written; an absent key leaves the broker's own behaviour.

order.description: Host slugs to try first, in this order, before the broker's own ranking. Soft: with allow_fallbacks the rest are still tried.

only.description: Allowlist of upstream host slugs; a base slug matches every region and variant, a full slug such as deepinfra/turbo pins one endpoint. A HARD filter, and the residency pin.

ignore.description: Blocklist of upstream host slugs. A HARD filter, for excluding one endpoint measured bad rather than for choosing among the rest.

allow_fallbacks.description: Whether the broker may switch hosts when the chosen one fails. Omit to keep its own default of true; false trades availability for the certainty of one host.

require_parameters.description: Route only to hosts supporting every parameter the request carries, so a structured-output call never reaches a host that ignores response_format.

data_collection.description: deny keeps the request off hosts that may store or train on prompts; allow (the broker's default) permits them.

zdr.description: Zero data retention: only hosts that keep no copy of the prompt or the answer may serve the request.

enforce_distillable_text.description: Only models whose licence allows their output to be used to train other models.

quantizations.description: Serving precisions a host may use. A HARD filter, and what makes repeated calls comparable: two answers from one model id at fp4 and at bf16 are two different models for every purpose except billing.

sort.description: Order candidate hosts by throughput, price or latency. The lever that collapses the latency tail, and it disables the broker's load balancing, which is the trade. Write {by, partition: none} to sort across every model of a fallback list at once.

max_price.description: The most a request may cost: USD per million prompt or completion tokens, or per request or image. Hosts above it are filtered out.

preferred_min_throughput.description: Prefer hosts producing at least this many tokens per second: one number for every percentile, or {p50, p75, p90, p99}. SOFT: a slower host is moved down the list, never removed.

preferred_max_latency.description: Prefer hosts answering within this many seconds: one number for every percentile, or {p50, p75, p90, p99}. SOFT: it reorders and never excludes, so it cannot bound a tail on its own.

openRouterReasoning.description: OpenRouter's reasoning request object: how hard a reasoning model thinks. Unset leaves each host its own default. effort and max_tokens are two ways to set one budget, so only one may be written.

effort.description: The thinking budget as a level. Halves latency and cost at low, and cost a fifth of the certification score on a drafting task, so set it where throughput dominates.

max_tokens.description: The thinking budget in tokens, for models that take one.

exclude.description: Think, but leave the reasoning text out of the answer.

enabled.description: Turn thinking on at the model's default budget, or off on a model that allows it.

connectionUpstream.description: Which upstream hosts may read every request on this provider, and under what privacy. Only the connection keys of openRouterProvider; how each tier is served stays on its routing. The flat spelling (only, ignore, allow_fallbacks at top level) is still read.

upstreamRoutingFlat.description: The older flat spelling of upstreamRouting, still read at every door and written nested on the next save that needs a field it lacks. Which of a broker's upstream hosts may serve this tier. OpenRouter fronts many inference hosts per model, and its own default picks among them weighted by the inverse square of price — so one model id is served at fp4 on one call and at bf16 on the next, with latency to match. Valid ONLY on an openai_compatible binding whose base_url is an OpenRouter host; the parser refuses it anywhere else rather than send a vendor fields it never asked for. OMIT the block to inherit the product default (sort: throughput, quantizations: [fp16, bf16], require_parameters: true — reliability over price); write an empty object to opt out and take the broker's own price-weighted routing. Measured 2026-09-02 — see docs/explanation/openrouter-upstream-choice.md.

sort.description: Order candidate hosts by throughput, price or latency. This is the lever that collapses the latency tail, and it disables the broker's load balancing, which is the trade. throughput measured best; latency reached slower hosts; price is roughly what the unpinned default already does.

quantizations.description: Serving precisions a host may use. A HARD filter, and what makes repeated calls comparable: two answers from one model id at fp4 and at bf16 are two different models for every purpose except billing.

require_parameters.description: Route only to hosts supporting every parameter the request carries. Belt-and-braces for a structured-output call: a soft preference already covers response_format most of the time, and this makes it a rule.

only.description: Allowlist of upstream host slugs; a base slug matches every region and variant, a full slug such as deepinfra/turbo pins one endpoint. A HARD filter. Prefer sort — pinning by slug reaches the same host while throwing away the failover breadth a sort leaves intact.

ignore.description: Blocklist of upstream host slugs. A HARD filter, for excluding one endpoint measured bad rather than for choosing among the rest.

allow_fallbacks.description: Whether the broker may switch hosts when the chosen one fails. Omit to keep its own default of true; set false only when a compliance rule or a measurement run demands a single host, because it trades availability for certainty.

preferred_max_latency_p90.description: Deprioritize hosts whose p90 latency over a rolling five-minute window exceeds this many seconds. SOFT: it reorders and never excludes, so it cannot bound a tail. Measured on its own it was worse than setting nothing — p90 43.7s, including one 231s call. Omit it, or 0, to leave it unset: once this binding has round-tripped through the settings store as JSON a written 0 and an absent key are the same value, so the runtime reads both as unset and this schema may not pretend otherwise.

reasoning_effort.description: Cap a reasoning model's thinking budget. Unset means each host applies its own default. Halves latency and cost, and cost a fifth of the certification score on a drafting task, so set it where throughput dominates rather than by default.

embeddingsBinding.description: The embeddings-lane binding: $defs/binding plus dimensions (a width only this lane has) and minus input (this lane sends no attachments). Two lanes with different fields, so each gets its own $def rather than one widened additionalProperties:false that would accept either field on either lane.

provider.description: fake | anthropic | ollama | vllm | openai_compatible | openai | gemini | gemini_vertex. The only place vendor names appear.

model.description: Provider-native model id. ollama/vllm default to a Gemma-class model when omitted (A23).

base_url.description: A separate embeddings server for this lane alone (vLLM serves one model per process). Empty ⇒ the provider's host (providers.<name>.base_url).

location.description: gemini_vertex only: a location of this lane's own, since Vertex serves an embedding model at fewer locations than a chat model. Empty ⇒ the provider's (providers.gemini_vertex.location).

dimensions.description: Vector width the provider is asked to emit. Optional; 0 or omitted defaults to 1536.

decisionsBinding.description: The decisions-lane binding: a provider that answers the decision wire, its model and its endpoint. No input and no routing: the lane sends no attachments and the decisions endpoint takes no broker preferences.

provider.description: jev (TypeSafe's own API; key TYPESAFE_API_KEY, required; base_url optional, default https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone) | jev_compatible (any server on the Jev wire: a broker such as OpenRouter, or a self-hosted server; key JEV_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY, sent when set and never required; base_url required).

model.description: The decision model id, e.g. jev-1.13.0 on jev, or typesafe/jev-1.13 on OpenRouter.

base_url.description: Deprecated here: set the endpoint on providers.<name>.base_url. Still accepted (the FULL decision endpoint URL, posted to as written) and lifted onto the provider when it names none.

embeddingsRouting.description: Which of a broker's upstream hosts may read the text this lane embeds, and under what privacy: the connection keys, which the lane may state for itself. The other upstreamRouting fields bound a completion's tail, which a single forward pass does not have. Valid only on an openai_compatible binding whose base_url is an OpenRouter host. Omit it to read the connection's.
